dossier.public_summary: This is not a planet but the star's own variability. The dip alternates deep and shallow every orbit and matches the star's 0.79-day spot period with huge brightness swings, and the implied size is stellar. The star itself shows signs of a close binary, so the dips are stellar eclipses/variability on the target.

reasons.why: odd and even transits differ by 12% (306400 ppm vs 269600 ppm) at ~46 sigma, positive in all sectors (sector_oe_max_sigma 77.84, sector_oe_same_sign_share 1) — indicates a binary at twice the period, not a planet
undiluted radius 0.5507 R* implies 33.11 Rearth on the M dwarf (stellar_radius Gaia FLAME gives 42.68-43.32 Rearth), well above the planetary regime (>22 Rearth) and stellar

rotation period 0.794 d equals the transit period with false_alarm 1.41e-30 and amplitudes 191948-237067 ppm (~100% of the dip depth 302703 ppm) — the large phase-curve swing and matching period show the dip is stellar variability, not a transit
extreme V shape favours grazing binary over planet

dip is on the target (offset 0.06673 arcsec) ruling out a neighbour, but Gaia RV rv_amplitude 212.1 km/s and ruwe 1.204 with Gaia EB match 0.000005746 point to the variability/binary being on the target
